subject: Bridgewell SIG3 follow-up: subprocessor delegation and dataflow ownership

From: Bridgewell Security <security@bridgewell.com>

Cc: AuditRepo Evidence Team <evidence@auditrepo.io>
Date: Sat, 22 Mar 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: SIG3 follow-up: subprocessor list + delegation letters

Hi Naomi,

Thanks for taking the SIG3. A couple follow-ups from our intake review: we need a current, itemized subprocessor roster that includes:
- provider name and legal entity
- function (e.g., telemetry, storage, KMS)
- geographic residency of data processing (country/region)
- whether they have delegated access to production systems (yes/no)

We also need any delegation letters (or equivalent contractual addenda) for subprocessors that have access to Bridgewell customer data, plus a short dataflow diagram showing where Bridgewell customer data traverses third parties. If you can provide a bundle (CSV + PDFs + diagram link) by EOD Tuesday 3/25 that would keep us on schedule.

If anything is sensitive, please flag and we can set up a secure transfer via the AuditRepo upload link.

Thanks,
Thomas Lee
Senior Information Security Analyst
Bridgewell Health

Thomas, Naomi —

Link to simplified dataflow diagram (read-only): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-bridgewell-evidence

A couple of clarifications to call out in the bundle:
- Transitive access: our inference runtime uses a feature-store partner (FeatureGrid Inc.) that writes hashed telemetry to an analytics tenant. FeatureGrid does not have plaintext Bridgewell identifiers but does receive hashed metadata (pseudonymous). That is documented in the CSV in the "notes" column.
- KMS: most production model keys are in our managed KMS (region: us-west-2). For customers who opt-in to private deployments we provide customer-managed key integration; the spreadsheet column "kms_owner" indicates which model groups are under Redwood-managed KMS vs customer KMS.
- Delegation letters: we use the attached template for subprocessors with admin-level or production-access roles. For subprocessors that only process telemetry or aggregate metrics we rely on contract addenda rather than full delegation letters.

If Bridgewell needs formal notarized delegation letters for any vendor, let us know which vendors and we can initiate that process (it takes ~5 business days for collection + signature).

Regards,
Jonas Weber
Senior Trust Engineer
Redwood Inference
